fields.features_heading: The Parts That Turn a Visit Into a Trial
fields.features_subheading: A free trial landing page turns a visitor into a trial user. These six parts make the offer plain and every start countable.
fields.feature_1:
One prompt for the offer and the form

Tell Emergent the trial length, whether it takes a card, and the price after. It builds the page and its signup form, with a table behind them, and you change it by prompting again.
fields.feature_2:
A signup form cut to what day one needs

Ask for the fields the first session uses, such as email and company, and nothing else. Each extra field is one more question a visitor answers before the product ever loads.
fields.feature_3:
Every trial saved with where it started

Each signup lands as a row in a database you own, with the time, the button the visitor pressed, and the page it sat on. Read the rows by week to see which button earns its spot.
fields.feature_4:
A reminder before each trial ends

Ask for an email that goes out a few days before a trial ends, with the trial's end date and the price that follows. The app sends it from the same table that saved the signup.
fields.feature_5:
Billing and CRM tools, connected

Connect the signup table to Stripe, HubSpot, or any tool with an API. A new trial can open a customer record in the billing tool and add a contact to the CRM as the row is saved.
fields.feature_6:
Code that leaves with you

Paid plans export the code for the page and its trial table to your GitHub repository. Or keep it hosted on Emergent on a custom domain, which uses credits, and edit by prompt.

fields.tab_content_1:
Two fields, then straight into the product

Harlowe sells scheduling software to tutors and runs a 14-day trial with no card. Its signup form has 2 fields, email and company, and the lesson calendar opens as soon as the form is sent. Of the 47 trials started this week, 29 came from the header button and 18 from the pricing link.
fields.tab_content_2:
On card trials, $29 and day 8 sit by the form

Quillbrook sells photo proofing to wedding photographers, and its 7-day trial takes a card. The $29 a month price sits beside the button, with one line under it: "Card charged on day 8 unless you cancel." The button opens the checkout of the billing tool Quillbrook connects.
fields.tab_content_3:
One pass, 3 visits, 7 days to use them

Kelswick Climbing gives first-timers a pass good for 3 visits in 7 days. The form asks for a name and an email, and the pass arrives by email with its own code. A screen at the front desk lists every pass: 21 claimed this week, 13 of them already used for a first visit.
fields.tab_content_4:
58 trials for headline B, 38 for the original

Saltmere, a newsletter tool for food bloggers, served two headlines on the same page for 2 weeks and counted trial starts for each. Headline B started 58 of the 96 trials, and the original started 38. Saltmere made headline B the only version and moved the next test to the button label.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Free Trial Landing Page
fields.howto_description: These 7 steps take a free trial landing page from one offer sentence to a published page that counts every trial start.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write the offer in one sentence
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide whether the trial takes a card
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only what the first screen needs
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Put the price where the form is
fields.howto_step_1_des: Put the trial length, the card rule, and the price after it into one line. For example: "14 days free, no card, then $19 a month." If a colleague has to read that line twice, rewrite it before you build anything around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A no-card trial asks only for the signup fields. With a card trial, the visitor adds payment details first, and you set in the billing tool what happens when the trial ends. Pick one model per offer and name it beside the button.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List what the product needs to open its first screen, which may be nothing more than an email. Ask for that alone. Phone numbers and team size can wait until the visitor is inside the product and has a reason to answer.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Place the plan's monthly cost after the trial where the visitor can see it while filling in the form, not on a separate pricing page. On a card trial, add the charge day under the button in plain words.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Show the first screen of the product
fields.howto_step_5_des: Use a screenshot or a short loop of the screen a new user lands on right after signing up. A visitor who can see that screen knows what the trial gives them before they type an email address.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Draft the emails around the end date
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the welcome email and the one sent before the trial ends, naming the date and the amount. If Stripe bills your trials, its hosted reminder emails are sent 7 days before the trial ends: time yours so the two do not arrive together.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish and count trials by source
fields.howto_step_7_des: Put the page on a custom domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits, and save each trial with the button or link it came from. Change one thing at a time, such as the headline, and give each version 2 full weeks.

faq_plan.q: What is a free trial landing page?
faq_plan.a: A free trial landing page is a page with one job: getting a visitor to start a trial of a product. It carries one signup form and one button, and it states the trial length, whether a card is needed, and the price after the trial before the visitor types anything.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a free trial landing page?
faq_plan.a: Settle the terms before the layout. Then describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder, naming the trial length, the fields the form needs, and where trials should be counted. It builds the page and the signup table, and you change either one by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a free trial signup form ask for?
faq_plan.a: An email address, plus anything the product cannot start without, such as a workspace name for a team tool. A password can wait until the email is confirmed. On a page built with Emergent, the free trial signup form saves each entry to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How is a free trial landing page different from a homepage?
faq_plan.a: A homepage serves every visitor, from buyers to job seekers, and links everywhere. A free trial landing page has one goal, the trial start, and drops the navigation that leads away from it. A saas landing page can do either job; the trial version keeps one form and one button.

faq_plan.q: Should a free trial landing page ask for a credit card?
faq_plan.a: Not by default. Leave the card off when visitors need to use the product before they decide to pay. Ask for it when every trial should end with a payment method on file. If traffic allows, run each model for 2 weeks and compare paid plans at the end, not trial starts.

faq_plan.q: How many days should the trial on a free trial landing page last?
faq_plan.a: As many days as a new user needs to reach the result the product promises at least once, plus a few to spare. Time how long that takes a real tester. A tool used once a week needs a longer trial than one used every hour. Put the length in the headline or right under it.

faq_plan.q: Can a free trial landing page send signups to a CRM?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the CRM has an API. An app built with Emergent can create the contact as each trial is saved, tagged with the button it came from, so sales can see which trials started on the pricing link. A crm landing page uses the same setup when the CRM is the product being sold.

faq_plan.q: What should a free trial landing page say about the end of the trial?
faq_plan.a: The date the trial ends, the price that follows, and whether the plan renews without the visitor doing anything. If the trial takes a card, add how and where to cancel. Keep it to one sentence near the form, in the same type size as the rest of the page.

faq_plan.q: How do I measure free trial landing page conversions?
faq_plan.a: Divide trial starts by unique visitors for the same period, and split both by source. Then track how many trials become paid plans. A page that starts more trials can still start fewer paying ones, and the paid count is the one that decides which version stays.

faq_plan.q: Should a free trial landing page for a developer tool look different?
faq_plan.a: It should lead with different proof. Put a code sample or the install command near the top, and start the trial with an account and an API key instead of a long form. A developer landing page covers that audience in more depth. On paid plans, Emergent exports the page's code to your GitHub repository.

plan.angle: The SERP for free trial landing page is example galleries (Unbounce, Instapage, Swipe Pages, Apexure), a wireframe template on Pinterest and a Reddit thread asking for conversion numbers: plenty of screenshots, but none of them say what the signup form should ask, whether to take a card, or what the page must say about the day the trial ends. This page shows four free trial landing pages where the offer is explicit (trial length, card or no card, the price after) and every trial start is saved with the place it came from, then builds them. SaaS, demo, startup, pricing-page and lead-generation landing pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Free Trial Landing Page That Spells Out the Offer'; hero 'Build a free trial landing page with a two-field signup, the price after the trial, and trials saved to a database you own.' (D1 clean); how-to description one sentence under 140 chars.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is example galleries and conversion questions; page gives four worked examples (No-Card Trial, Card-Up-Front Trial, Gym Trial Pass, Headline Test), a 7-step how-to and 'How do I measure free trial landing page conversions?'.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'Card charged on day 8 unless you cancel', 'the price after the trial', 'trial starts by source'; table column uses the campaign-page variant 'Prompt for a campaign page'.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Tell Emergent the trial length...', 'Harlowe sells scheduling software to tutors...', 'Put the trial length, the card rule, and the price after it into one line.'

craft.evidence: One ', so' ending on the page (FAQ 7), under the cap; sentences carry one idea each, e.g. 'Headline B started 58 of the 96 trials, and the original started 38.'

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous details: 'a pass good for 3 visits in 7 days', '21 claimed this week, 13 of them already used for a first visit'; no AI tells.

truth.evidence: Stripe line 'its hosted reminder emails are sent 7 days before the trial ends' matches the quoted span on docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/trials ('Stripe-hosted reminder emails are sent 7 days before the trial ends.'); Emergent claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, api-connect, code-export, custom-domain; numbers add up (29+18=47, 58+38=96, 21-13=8).

distinct.evidence: Own angle (card rule, price after the trial, end-date reminder); sibling primaries appear only as FAQ link anchors ('saas landing page', 'crm landing page', 'developer landing page'), not headings.
